To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a novel regret minimization (RG) framework for generalizing across multiple environments and that we extend RG for environments defined by complex descriptors.

we introduce a novel regret minimization algorithm and a structured extension for structured environments that significantly outperforms state of the art methods in a variety of biomedical applications.

we introduce RGM, a regret minimization algorithm for predictive invariant risk minimization, that is able to generalize to environments not seen during training and that outperforms previous methods on molecular property prediction, homology prediction and stability prediction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a novel algorithm for generalization across environments.
developing a new regret minimisation algorithm for structured environments, and its application in multiple domains.
developing new methods for generalizing to unseen environments, and we hope that our results motivate future research in this direction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is the state-of-the-art for the considered applications.
our method is able to outperform previous state-of-the-arts on multiple applications and domains.
RGM is a novel algorithm that is able to learn invariance and generalize to unseen environments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we introduce a novel algorithm for learning invariant predictors across complex structured environments.
we propose a new algorithm for learning predictive invariance across structured biomedical domains.
we propose a novel algorithm that can learn a model which is simultaneously optimal for all environments, including unseen environments, and can be applied to structured domains.
The main takeaway from our work is that
predictive invariance is a powerful tool to enforce generalization across structured domains.
predictive invariance can be a useful tool for generalization beyond the training environment in structured domains, where most environments are never seen or contain only one training example.
by leveraging the structure of the environment, we can significantly improve generalization in structured domains.
